procedure_text: NMST (20g, 0.088mol), sodium hypochlorite (150ml, 0.222mol) and ruthenium oxide (0.5g, 0.004mol) were charged into a 500ml round bottomed flask. This mixture was heated to reflux temperature under stirring for 6-8 hours, cooled to 25-30°C and filtered. The filtrate obtained was further cooled to 5-10°C and acidified to pH < 3 using concentrated hydrochloric acid (54mL, 0.51mol) to form precipitated product (NMSBA). The product obtained was filtered and dried at 50°C under reduced pressure to obtain NMSBA as light yellow solid. HPLC purity >95%; Yield: 68%; and Melting point: 210-214°C.
procedure_summary: NMST is oxidised at its methyl group to NMSBA with sodium hypochlorite over a ruthenium oxide catalyst, the mixture being held at reflux and then cooled and filtered to remove the catalyst. The filtrate is cooled further and acidified with concentrated hydrochloric acid to precipitate the product, which is filtered and dried under reduced pressure.

ARITHMETIC. Tested on the run's convention, the MASS-PRECISION test: propagate the significant figures of the printed mass to a mole interval and raise molar_mass_inconsistent only where the printed mole figure falls outside that interval, so both printed numbers are treated with the precision they are actually printed with. One of the two printed mass/mole pairs passes and one fails. RUTHENIUM OXIDE PASSES: 0.5 g is one significant figure, so it stands for 0.45 to 0.55 g, which at 133.068 g/mol for RuO2 gives 0.00338 to 0.00413 mol, and that interval contains the printed 0.004 mol. NMST FAILS: the mass is printed "20", not "20.0", so it carries two significant figures and stands for 19.5 to 20.5 g, which at 215.230 g/mol for C8H9NO4S gives 0.09060 to 0.09525 mol; the printed 0.088 mol lies outside that interval, so the pair cannot be reconciled at the precision the patent prints and molar_mass_inconsistent is raised. This is the widest interval of the three NMST charges in the document, and the printed figure is excluded even at that width, which makes the finding stronger rather than weaker. Reaching the same conclusion by the cruder route: 20 g / 0.088 mol implies 227.3 g/mol, which never reaches 215.23 g/mol, and 20 g is in truth 0.0929 mol, so the printed mole figure is about 5.3% low. Every interval and implied weight here is a recomputation of mine, not a number the patent prints, and none of them entered any structured field. Nothing is corrected. Example 1 shows the same defect in the same direction on the same compound and Example 2 does not, so it is neither universal in the document nor unique to this section; of the pairs tested across the run this one is the clearest failure. mass_balance_implausible is NOT raised: the patent prints a 68% yield but no isolated product mass, so there is no printed mass to test against the input moles and no stated pair that disagrees. The hypochlorite is a solution volume with a mole figure and the acid likewise, so neither admits a molecular-weight check; both are consistent in concentration with the other Examples.

CATALYST CHARGE. 0.5 g of ruthenium oxide is charged here at 20 g of NMST and Example 2 charges the same 0.5 g at 5.0 g of NMST, a fourfold difference in loading between two Examples of one procedure. No validation flag covers a loading difference between sections and none was invented for it; scale_discontinuity is about a step's input against the previous step's output, which is not this.
